digest.component_or_area: completion-verifier agentic LLM step, tool-call loop detection and actuator
propositions: A repeating tool-call cycle in the completion-verify step burns the entire request budget (240 requests) and is killed with no verdict instead of landing a verdict on collected evidence; four independent tool-loop captures (aec1, 895c, e369, and 8b97) all died budget-exhausted with max_consecutive_repeat underreporting non-adjacent cycles.

The actuator (tool_step_limit and withdrawal) exists but is wired only to bounded recovery (16 steps), not to the primary verify step; build_agent_request never sets tool_step_limit for the primary verify step, so no forced landing occurs despite the shipped mechanism.

The existing repetition detector max_consecutive_repeat is blind to cycles of length >= 2 and scores healthy breadth higher than pathological runs; a windowed distinct-ratio (24-call window, trip <= 0.50) correctly separates the three pathological runs (ratios 0.119, 0.290, 0.511) from healthy runs (ratio >= 0.833).

When budget exhaustion raises UsageLimitExceeded, interpret_failure computes a repetition diagnostic but raises LLMRunnerError, which CompletionAgentStep.run does not catch (only UnretryableOutputError); bounded recovery is unreachable and no verdict is emitted.

The tool-withdrawal mechanism (filtering toolset on run_step <= limit) is protocol-unsafe on Bedrock/Anthropic (omits toolConfig while history contains toolUse blocks, triggering ValidationException 400); synthetic tool-result steering (call_tool returns a steering notice) replaces it to keep tool definitions advertised while stopping execution.
